Where to start

What type of company should you register?

Each structure balances ownership, liability and compliance differently. Here is a plain-language view of the common options.

Popular for startups

Private Limited Company

Suitable for startups and growing businesses that plan to hire, sign contracts or raise investment.

  • Separate legal entity
  • Limited liability
  • Equity is fundable and transferable

Limited Liability Partnership (LLP)

Suitable for professional services and partner-managed businesses that want formal structure with lighter compliance.

  • Partner-based management
  • Limited liability
  • Lighter statutory compliance

One Person Company (OPC)

Suitable for solo founders who want a formal company without a co-founder requirement.

  • Single member
  • Limited liability
  • Incorporated identity

Partnership Firm

Suitable for small teams who want to share ownership and profits without full incorporation.

  • Shared ownership and profits
  • Unincorporated, simple to run
  • Partners generally bear personal liability

Sole Proprietorship

For individuals running a business in their own name, with no legal separation between owner and business.

  • Single owner
  • No incorporation required
  • Owner bears personal liability

Section 8 Company

For charitable, educational or social initiatives — a non-profit company that cannot distribute profits.

  • Non-profit objectives
  • Limited liability
  • No dividend distribution

Not sure which structure fits your situation? Options depend on your goals and circumstances — a registration advisor can help you compare quickly.

The real work

Why registration takes more than filling a form

Incorporation is a sequence of regulated steps. Each one can stall your application if it isn’t handled carefully — and the gaps show up later.

01

Choosing the wrong structure

Your entity follows your business for years. A mismatch surfaces later — in compliance costs, investor appetite, or the difficulty of restructuring.

02

A name that doesn’t clear

Rejected or disputed names mean rework and delay before your application ever moves forward.

03

Gaps in director & KYC details

Identity, address, consent and appointment details must align with the structure you choose. Errors here are a common review point.

04

Documentation that doesn’t hold up

Incomplete or inconsistent documents are a leading cause of deficiencies and re-submission.

05

Filing mistakes & regulator queries

Errors in applications attract queries that slow the process down — and each round-trip takes time.

06

Stopping at the certificate

PAN, TAN and compliance registrations follow incorporation. Companies that overlook them face penalties.

That’s what ArthoVista coordinates. You stay informed at each stage — structure, documentation, filing and follow-up — and always know where your application stands.

Questions

Frequently asked questions

Straight answers to the questions enterprises ask us most.

Which company structure should I choose?

It depends on your goals, team size, funding plans and how you want to manage liability. Private Limited companies suit startups planning to raise investment; LLPs suit professional and partner-managed businesses; OPCs suit solo founders; partnerships and proprietorships are simpler, unincorporated options. There is no single right answer — we help you compare what fits your situation.

How long does company registration take?

The timeline depends on the structure, the completeness of your documents and the processing times of the authorities — typically ranging from a few days to a few weeks. We give you a realistic timeline for your case once your documents are in place, rather than a generic promise.

What documents or information will I need?

The essentials are generally proof of identity and address for the founders or partners, and a registered office address in India. Some structures also need consent of directors and a Digital Signature Certificate for electronic filings. We prepare a personalised checklist based on your structure, so you are not guessing halfway through.

Can a single person register a company?

Yes. A One Person Company (OPC) allows a single member to incorporate with limited liability. If you want a Private Limited company, you generally need at least two directors, with one residing in India.

What is the difference between Private Limited, LLP and OPC?

Put simply: Private Limited is an incorporated company suited to equity-funded growth; LLP is an incorporated partnership suited to partner-managed practices with lighter compliance; OPC is a single-member incorporated company. They differ in ownership, liability, compliance and how investors typically view them.

Do I need a registered office address?

Yes — you generally need a registered office address in India where official communication can be served. Ownership or rental documentation is typically required to support it, and we guide you on what works for your situation.

Can ArthoVista guarantee that my registration will be approved?

No one can guarantee an outcome on your behalf — approval depends on the submitted documents and the decision of the authorities. What we can do is prepare your documentation properly, check it carefully and coordinate the process, so your application is in the strongest form it can be.

What happens after I submit my enquiry?

We review your enquiry, a registration advisor reaches out during business hours to understand your situation, and you receive a clear recommendation on structure plus a tailored document checklist. There is no obligation to proceed.

Can an existing informal business get help formalising?

Yes. If you are already operating — as a sole proprietorship, partnership or unregistered business — we help you understand what formalising would mean for your situation, including the right structure and the steps involved.

What happens after registration?

Registration is the starting line. You receive your incorporation documents and a plain-language view of the compliance that follows, so you know what comes next. If you need deeper support — certifications, funding or growth — ArthoVista offers those services too.
